correctness.rationale: Proved point-character criterion for literal unrestricted two-round EF game, together with a deterministic exact append transition on 32-bit type masks. Breadth-first closure of all reachable types gives 97 states, all 194 append edges internally checked; 90 use both letters. Reversal involution fixes 20; exhaustive symmetric-word generation through length nine realizes all 20. Each palindrome and unrestricted representative is additionally checked by a separately written literal game solver. Two length-nine words have eight distinct characters and two self-dual characters, implying that a palindrome cannot have eight or fewer positions in their classes. No extrapolation from finite experiments is used: complete transition closure proves all-length exhaustiveness.

value.rationale: Palindrome realizability is a natural symmetry-satisfiability property not expressible as a single bounded-rank condition on each word. Complete classification of its intersections with logical two-round types, a precise iff test, and the one-position gap between unrestricted and symmetry-constrained optimal models give concrete finite-model and formal-language information. The two extreme examples exhibit a structural parity obstruction via self-dual pointed characters; the result is not merely the earlier known count of 90.
